agent_review.notes: All five criteria met on a live claude-code turn. The pane's longest line is 120 chars (its wrap width) while the extracted reply's longest line is 186 — the authored line, unbroken — so the answer came from the JSONL transcript, not the screen. (1) Both paragraph breaks survive as blank lines. (2) Three list items, each on its own line with its '- ' marker. (3) No break inside any sentence. (4) Directly renderable markdown. (5) Wording, the FMT_ token and punctuation unchanged. This is the provider whose gap was subtlest: claude ALREADY preferred its transcript, but gated on `len(transcript) > len(pane)`, which repairs truncation and is blind to re-wrapping — wrapping swaps a space for a newline, so both forms are the SAME length and the longer-is-better test never fired. It now routes through llmtypes.ReconcileFinalAnswer, which compares by words instead. Provenance: the first live run of this test failed for an unrelated reason worth recording — claude declined the task, reading the random FMT_ token as an identifier it needed real knowledge about. The prompt was reframed as an explicit echo/formatting exercise, which is also more robust across providers.
